# CLI reference

Every command's `--help`. The global `--config` option applies to all of them.

## awaywork

```text
Usage: awaywork [options] [command]

Spend idle coding-subscription quota while you're away

Options:
  -V, --version             output the version number
  -c, --config <path>       config file (default: $AWAYWORK_CONFIG or
                            ~/.config/awaywork/config.yml)
  -h, --help                display help for command

Commands:
  init [options]            detect installed agents, pick providers, sources and
                            a starting queue
  config                    print the config schema or edit the config
  plan [options]            show the next run's units in order, with each
                            provider's ceiling; runs no worker; browsable in a
                            terminal
  skip [options] [key]      leave an item (source:key, e.g. github:acme/api#5)
                            alone in the coming runs; with no key, list skipped
                            items
  unskip <key>              let awaywork pick up a skipped item (source:key)
                            again
  approve <key> [notes...]  approve the plan an item (source:key, e.g.
                            github:acme/api#5) waits on, replying approve on it
                            with the notes below; otherwise mark it approved,
                            for rules with `where: { approved: true }`, until a
                            unit on it finishes
  skills                    list skills and eject built-ins to tweak
  run [options]             plan the units, start a worker per unit and publish
                            PRs and reports
  report [options] [id]     print a run's morning report, the latest by default;
                            browsable in a terminal
  watch                     keep running and start a run when a window opens;
                            `schedule install` keeps it running
  stats [options]           what each rule, skill and provider cost and
                            delivered across the runs kept
  replay <run> <unit>       re-run a past run's unit, its first step, on its
                            base commit and saved context with today's skills
                            and instructions; nothing is pushed
  schedule                  run awaywork when its windows open, on this machine
                            or in GitHub Actions
  doctor [options]          validate the config and check binaries, credentials,
                            quota and sources before a run
  help [command]            display help for command
```

## awaywork init

```text
Usage: awaywork init [options]

detect installed agents, pick providers, sources and a starting queue

Options:
  -y, --yes             answer every question with its default; needs no
                        terminal
  --provider <id...>    with --yes: providers, first takes units first
  --source <id...>      with --yes: sources to take work from
  --window <start-end>  with --yes: the run window, e.g. 01:00-07:00
  --force               replace an existing config without asking
  -h, --help            display help for command
```

## awaywork config

```text
Usage: awaywork config [options] [command]

print the config schema or edit the config

Options:
  -h, --help      display help for command

Commands:
  schema          print the config JSON Schema, for editor autocompletion
  edit            open the config in $VISUAL or $EDITOR; it is saved only once
                  valid
  help [command]  display help for command
```

## awaywork plan

```text
Usage: awaywork plan [options]

show the next run's units in order, with each provider's ceiling; runs no
worker; browsable in a terminal

Options:
  --json            print the plan and warnings as JSON
  --repo <glob>     only units in repos matching owner/name, * globs
  --rule <n>        only units of this queue rule, counted from 1
  --rules           show what each rule takes now and what earlier rules take
                    from it, instead of the units; probes no provider
  --skipped [kind]  list the skipped items and why, or those of one kind
                    (choices: "no_rule", "skipped_by_you", "unchanged",
                    "over_cap", "waiting_for_review", "waiting_for_answer",
                    "waiting_for_approval", "invalid_plan", "fanned_out",
                    "waiting_for_task", "task_merged", "task_done",
                    "all_tasks_done", "gave_up", "no_repo", "invalid_branch",
                    "refused_delivery", "unstackable", "running")
  --why <key>       say why an item is planned or skipped, by key, source:key or
                    the ref plan shows
  -h, --help        display help for command
```

## awaywork skip

```text
Usage: awaywork skip [options] [key]

leave an item (source:key, e.g. github:acme/api#5) alone in the coming runs;
with no key, list skipped items

Options:
  --until <date>   skip until this local date (YYYY-MM-DD) starts; default:
                   until unskip
  --reason <text>  why, shown by awaywork plan
  -h, --help       display help for command
```

## awaywork unskip

```text
Usage: awaywork unskip [options] <key>

let awaywork pick up a skipped item (source:key) again

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command
```

## awaywork approve

```text
Usage: awaywork approve [options] <key> [notes...]

approve the plan an item (source:key, e.g. github:acme/api#5) waits on, replying
approve on it with the notes below; otherwise mark it approved, for rules with
`where: { approved: true }`, until a unit on it finishes

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command
```

## awaywork skills

```text
Usage: awaywork skills [options] [command]

```

## awaywork run

```text
Usage: awaywork run [options]

plan the units, start a worker per unit and publish PRs and reports

Options:
  --dry-run      prepare each workspace (clone, context, prompt) but run no
                 worker
  --unit <id>    run only this unit, by id or item key
  --repo <glob>  run only units in repos matching owner/name, * globs
  --rule <n>     run only units of this queue rule, counted from 1
  --scheduled    run only inside a window and start no unit after it ends
  -h, --help     display help for command
```

## awaywork report

```text
Usage: awaywork report [options] [id]

print a run's morning report, the latest by default; browsable in a terminal

Options:
  --list            list the last 20 runs: units, PRs and reports
  --json            print the run's results as JSON instead of the text
  --unit <n|key>    show one unit in full, by its number in the report, unit id
                    or item key
  --skipped [kind]  list the skipped items, or those of one kind (choices:
                    "no_rule", "skipped_by_you", "unchanged", "over_cap",
                    "waiting_for_review", "waiting_for_answer",
                    "waiting_for_approval", "invalid_plan", "fanned_out",
                    "waiting_for_task", "task_merged", "task_done",
                    "all_tasks_done", "gave_up", "no_repo", "invalid_branch",
                    "refused_delivery", "unstackable", "running")
  -h, --help        display help for command
```

## awaywork schedule

```text
Usage: awaywork schedule [options] [command]

run awaywork when its windows open, on this machine or in GitHub Actions

Options:
  -h, --help         display help for command

Commands:
  install [options]  keep `awaywork watch` running, which starts a run when a
                     window opens
  remove             remove the scheduled job, and
                     .github/workflows/awaywork.yml in the current repo
  status             show the installed scheduled job and what awaywork watch is
                     doing
  help [command]     display help for command
```

## awaywork schedule install

```text
Usage: awaywork schedule install [options]

keep `awaywork watch` running, which starts a run when a window opens

Options:
  --with <scheduler>  launchd, systemd, cron, github-actions (default: asks in a
                      terminal, else launchd on macOS, else systemd if it runs,
                      else cron)
  -h, --help          display help for command
```

## awaywork schedule remove

```text
Usage: awaywork schedule remove [options]

remove the scheduled job, and .github/workflows/awaywork.yml in the current repo

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command
```
